result.topic_en: Gauss defines a generalized hypergeometric-type series Ψ(α,β,γ,δ,x)=P, derives an inhomogeneous second-order differential equation it satisfies, transforms it by x = t/(t−1), finds this approach inconvenient, and turns to showing a property of a related finite/terminating series.
result.transcription:
Setzt man
$1+\frac{\alpha\beta}{\gamma\delta}x+\frac{\alpha.\alpha+1.\beta.\beta+1}{\gamma.\gamma+1.\delta.\delta+1}xx+\text{u.s.w.}=\Psi(\alpha.\beta.\gamma.\delta.x)$
$=P$
so ist
$(\alpha\beta-(\gamma-1)(\delta-1))P+((\alpha+\beta+1)x-(\gamma+\delta-1))P'+(xx-x)P''$ {+$\frac{dP}{dx}$+} {+$\frac{ddP}{dx^2}$+}
$=\frac{(\alpha\beta-\gamma\delta)(\gamma-1)(\delta-1)}{\gamma\delta}+\frac{\alpha\beta(\gamma-1)(\delta-1)((\alpha+1)(\beta+1)-(\gamma+1)(\delta+1))}{\gamma.\gamma+1.\delta.\delta+1}x$
$=A+Bx$
Schreibt man $x=\frac{t}{t-1}$
so wird die Gleichung
$\frac{\alpha\beta-(\gamma-1)(\delta-1)}{t-1}P-((\alpha+\beta-\gamma-\delta+2)t+\gamma+\delta-1)\frac{dP}{dt}$
$+(tt-t)\frac{ddP}{dt^2}$
$=\frac{-A+(A+B)t}{(t-1)^2}$
Diese Art führt nicht bequem zum Ziele. Wohl aber die auf S. 290 angedeutete
Es kommt nur darauf an zu zeigen, daß wenn die Reihe
$1-\frac{k(1-\theta)}{n+1}+\frac{k.k-1}{1.2.}\frac{1-\theta.2-\theta}{n+1.n+2}-\frac{k.k-1.k-2}{1.2.3}\frac{1-\theta.2-\theta.3-\theta}{n+1.n+2.n+3}$
$+\text{u.s.w}$
wo k eine ganze positive Zahl ist eben so wie n

methods.what: Definition of a generalized hypergeometric series with two numerator and two denominator parameters
Inhomogeneous second-order linear differential equation satisfied by the series P, with right side linear in x
Change of variable x = t/(t−1) transforming the differential equation
Terminating alternating binomial-hypergeometric series in k, θ, n to be studied
